title: The Efficacy and Safety of Dalfampridine on Cognition and Fatigue in People With Multiple Sclerosis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authors: Halabi MH, Alromayan R, Almutairi M, Alasmari H, AlGhamdi MA, Makkawi S
abstract: BACKGROUND: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic autoimmune disease affecting the central nervous system. People with MS frequently experience cognitive dysfunction and fatigue. Dalfampridine (DAL), a potassium channel blocker, is US Food and Drug Administration-approved for the treatment of walking impairment in people with MS. It may also enhance nerve conduction in regions associated with fatigue and cognitive dysfunction. This study aims to evaluate DAL's efficacy in improving these symptoms, as well as its safety profile, in people with MS. METHODS: A systematic search was conducted across MEDLINE, ScienceDirect, Scopus, Embase, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, and Web of Science, covering all records from database inception through April 1, 2024. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing DAL with placebo in people with MS and reporting impaired cognition and fatigue were included. A random-effects model was used to calculate the risk ratio (RR), standardized mean difference (SMD), and mean difference (MD) with 95% CIs. RESULTS: Of 1329 studies identified, 13 RCTs involving a total of 827 people with MS were included. DAL demonstrated a significant improvement in cognitive symptoms (SMD = 0.21; 95% CI, 0.04-0.38; P = .01; I² = 6%). However, no significant difference was observed between DAL and placebo in reducing fatigue (MD = 3.70; 95% CI, -4.37 to 11.77;P = .37; I² = 19%). Safety measures were comparable, with no significant difference in adverse events (RR = 1.11; 95% CI, 0.99-1.25; P = .08; I² = 0%). CONCLUSIONS: People with MS receiving DAL demonstrated significant improvement in cognitive symptoms; however, further studies are warranted to validate and confirm this finding.

title: Predicting IGD treatment outcomes across interventions using a whole-brain functional connectome biomarker.
authors: Wei M, Luo X, Fu J, Li S, Ni H, Liu J, Dong GH
abstract: BACKGROUND: Although treatment approaches have been explored in internet gaming disorder (IGD), however, little is known about the specific neural activity that is associated with treatment outcomes. This study aims to establish a treatment-sensitive network that reliably predicts treatment outcomes across different interventions for IGD. METHODS: Resting-state fMRI data were collected from 90 individuals with IGD who received one of three different intervention protocols (mindfulness meditation, approach bias modification, or retrieval-aversive conditioning training). Connectome-based predictive modelling (CPM) was used to build a treatment-sensitive network to predict individual symptom reduction, then validated them on the external dataset. RESULTS: The negative (r = 0.401, p <.001) and combined network (r = 0.480, p <.001) can significantly predict a reduction of addiction severity (baseline minus post-test). Specifically, the negative network was primarily centred on the motor, subcortical, and salience networks. The positive network primarily involved cerebellar-related connections. Incorporating these into a combined model significantly improved predictive accuracy, suggesting that cerebellar-related connectivity may contribute to the prediction of intervention-related clinical improvement. Finally, the treatment-sensitive network was validated in a separate data. CONCLUSIONS: This study established a treatment-sensitive network based on the whole-brain connectome. These findings provide valuable empirical evidence for identifying biomarkers for IGD treatment and advance personalised therapeutic strategies. CLINICAL TRIALS REGISTRATION: The trial protocol was pre-registered with the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (www.chictr.org.cn; ChiCTR2300077831(MM), ChiCTR2300075869(ApBm), ChiCTR2500095444(R-AC), ChiCTR2400090834(SAE)).

title: Evaluating a Modified American Society of Anesthesiologists Physical Status-Based Sedation Management System for Pancreatobiliary Endoscopy: A Prospective Feasibility Study.
authors: Hanaoka T, Okuwaki K, Watanabe M, Matsuda H, Adachi K, Tamaki A, Ogawa D, Sakai M
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To prospectively evaluate the feasibility of implementing a modified American Society of Anesthesiologists Physical Status (ASA-PS)-based sedation management system for endoscopist-managed sedation in pancreatobiliary endoscopy. METHODS: This single-center, single-arm prospective feasibility study involved 2000 patients (2024-2025). Sedation risk was stratified using a modified ASA-PS classification system combined with predefined high-risk clinical factors (severe obesity, obstructive sleep apnea requiring continuous positive airway pressure, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease requiring home oxygen therapy, reduced functional capacity, and difficult sedation history). Patients meeting high-risk criteria underwent pre-procedural anesthesiologist assessment to determine sedation providers. The primary outcome was sedation-related adverse event (SRAE) incidence during endoscopist-managed sedation. The secondary outcomes were the sedation success rate and SRAE-associated risk factors. RESULTS: Among 2000 patients, 231 (11.6%) were classified as having high risk for sedation. Post-assessment, anesthesiologists and endoscopists managed sedation for 86 (4.3%) and 1914 (95.7%) patients, respectively. In the endoscopist-managed group, SRAEs occurred in 63 patients (3.3%), corresponding to a success rate of 96.7%. No patient required tracheal intubation or conversion to general anesthesia. In multivariable analysis, endoscopic ultrasonography-guided sampling was independently associated with reduced SRAEs (odds ratio 0.407, 95% confidence interval 0.184-0.899; p = 0.026); no independent predictors of increased SRAEs were identified. CONCLUSIONS: The modified ASA-PS-based sedation management system may be a feasible approach in settings with limited anesthesiology resources, warranting further validation. TRIAL REGISTRATION: UMIN000053211.

title: Primary care effectiveness, multimorbidity, and hospital use in public and private health-care systems in Brazil: a cross-sectional analysis of data from the 2019-2021 Brazilian longitudinal study of aging.
authors: Oliveira GM, Nunes BP, Lam K, Lima-Costa MF, Torres JL, Macinko J, Moreira BS, Avelino-Silva TJ
abstract: BACKGROUND: Whether patient-reported experiences in primary care modify the association between multimorbidity and emergency department (ED) visits and hospitalizations remains unclear. We examined these associations across public and private health system sectors among Brazilians aged ≥50 years. METHODS: This cross-sectional study used nationally representative data from the 2019-2021 Brazilian Longitudinal Study of Aging. Multimorbidity was defined as the presence of ≥2 of 13 chronic conditions. A 12-item patient-reported primary care effectiveness index captured access, continuity, communication, and coordination with participants' usual source of healthcare. Primary outcomes were ED visits and hospitalizations in the past 12 months. Poisson regression models estimated associations with the outcomes, and assessed interactions among multimorbidity, primary care effectiveness, and health system sectors. FINDINGS: Among 9058 participants (mean age = 66.3 ± 9.9 years; females = 55.3%; White race/ethnicity = 46.4%), 38.0% had multimorbidity. Overall, 12.5% reported an ED visit and 6.0% ≥ 1 hospitalization in the past 12 months. Multimorbidity was associated with approximately twice the prevalence of ED visits and three times the prevalence of hospitalizations. Primary care effectiveness modified these associations across health system sectors (three-way interaction p = 0.04 for ED visits and p < 0.001 for hospitalization). In the public system, higher primary care effectiveness attenuated the association between multimorbidity and hospitalization (interaction prevalence ratio [PR] = 0.74, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 0.63-0.87). In contrast, in the private system, higher primary care effectiveness strengthened the associations of multimorbidity with ED visits (interaction PR = 1.40, 95% CI = 1.18-1.66) and hospitalization (interaction PR = 1.75, 95% CI = 1.22-2.50). INTERPRETATION: Associations between multimorbidity and healthcare use varied according to patient-reported primary care experiences and health system sector. FUNDING: The Brazilian National Council for Scientific and Technological Development, the Alzheimer's Association, and the National Institute on Aging.

title: A topologically engineered hydrogel platform targeting IL11 promotes renal repair after partial nephrectomy.
authors: Yu Z, Dong X, Li F, Zhang Y, Dai S, Cao N, Jia X, Zhao J
abstract: Partial nephrectomy (PN) is the gold standard for treating renal tumors and trauma; however, massive nephron loss and persistent fibrosis readily lead to chronic kidney disease (CKD). Current therapeutic options remain non-curative and costly, as nearly half of PN patients inevitably progress to end-stage renal failure. Here, we present an innovative regenerative platform for PN-induced CKD, integrating structural biomimicry with targeted molecular inhibition. Harnessing light-based bioprinting of gelatin and hyaluronic acid methacrylates coupled with removable alginate microfiber, we constructed a hierarchical channel scaffold (HCS) that features precisely patterned macrochannels and template-derived microchannels, which closely mimics native kidney architecture, provides structural support, and remarkably enhances cell migration (∼5.45-fold) and rapid neovascularization (∼7.66-fold) over unidirectional channel structures. Moreover, interleukin 11 (IL11) was identified as a novel therapeutic target in kidney fibrosis after PN. Thus, extracellular vesicles (EVs) derived from mesenchymal stem cells loaded with IL11 small interfering RNA (siIL11) were homogeneously encapsulated into HCS, achieving over 4-fold higher renal retention than systemic delivery in PN-induced CKD mice. Furthermore, sustained local release of EV-siIL11 and hierarchically channeled HCS guided synergistic regenerative effects that remarkably inhibited fibrosis, cell cycle arrest, and immune responses, thereby potently preventing kidney atrophy and restoring renal structure with newly aligned nephrons and vasculature, ultimately recovering kidney function. Further analysis revealed that IL11 silencing reversed epithelial‒mesenchymal transition by suppressing the STAT3-ERK-GSK3β-SNAI1 axis. This topological multifunctional hydrogel platform offers a localized, sustained, and clinically translatable strategy for postsurgical kidney regeneration.

title: Unsolved problems with ENaC: From molecules to mammals.
authors: Palmer LG
abstract: The epithelial Na channel (ENaC) mediates transport of Na+ in the kidney, the colon, the lung, and the sweat and salivary ducts. The activity of these channels is highly regulated and contributes to the maintenance of total body Na+, extracellular fluid volume, and plasma K+. Defects in the channel itself or in its regulation are implicated in hypertension and in other diseases. Despite progress in revealing many aspects of ENaC biology, many important questions remain unanswered. These include the following: What determines the remarkable ion selectivity of the channel? How is the channel directed to the apical plasma membrane? How does aldosterone regulate the channel? What is its role in producing urine with minimal Na+? And to what extent does the channel contribute to essential hypertension, cystic fibrosis, nephrotic syndrome, and liver failure? Here, I will discuss these questions and how they relate to our current understanding of the roles of ENaC in health and disease.

title: From animal behavior to human perioperative neurocognitive disorders: Translational boundaries of the gut-brain axis.
authors: Zhu C, Wei J
abstract: Perioperative neurocognitive disorders (PND), including postoperative delirium (POD), delayed neurocognitive recovery (DNR), and postoperative neurocognitive disorder, are common after surgery in older adults, and the gut-brain axis has been proposed as a contributing pathway. Most mechanistic support rests on rodent behavioral assays, yet these endpoints and human clinical diagnoses are routinely treated as interchangeable. This critical narrative review examines that translational boundary. PND is used here as a clinically consequential test case for a broader behavioral-neuroscience problem: how animal behavioral phenotypes, microbiome-associated signals, and intervention effects should be translated into human diagnostic constructs. A structured search identified and appraised the principal evidence rather than an exhaustive synthesis; no formal risk-of-bias or certainty-of-evidence assessment was performed. Evidence was separated into human perioperative studies reporting a neurocognitive outcome with either a measured gut-brain exposure or a gut-directed intervention; those reporting gut-brain change without a cognitive outcome; perioperative preclinical evidence; and indirect non-perioperative evidence. The retrieved human perioperative evidence spans observational cohorts across gastric, orthopedic, spinal and cardiac surgery, multi-omic and metabolomic cohorts, and randomized perioperative probiotic trials reporting lower rates of study-defined cognitive outcomes. It nonetheless remains heterogeneous and largely single-center, with modest event numbers, inconsistent sampling and assessment, and limited external validation. Mechanistic support still comes mainly from perioperative rodent models using water maze, fear-conditioning, recognition-memory, and delirium-like readouts, which measure narrow, species-specific capacities and are not diagnostic equivalents of POD, DNR, or postoperative neurocognitive disorder. Microbiome-mediated causation is unproven, and cross-species endpoint alignment remains a central route to improved translation.

title: Therapeutic Balloon-Assisted Enteroscopy: Recent Advances in the Management of Small Bowel Diseases.
authors: Nagayama M, Kinoshita T, Kawaguchi H, Fujinuma T, Fujikura S, Hayashi H, Tamaru T, Sakamoto H
abstract: Balloon-assisted enteroscopy (BAE) has substantially advanced small bowel disease management. This review summarizes recent therapeutic BAE advances, focusing on three major indications: small bowel vascular lesions, hereditary polyposis syndromes, and Crohn's disease (CD). For suspected small bowel bleeding from vascular lesions, morphological classification guides lesion-specific hemostasis-primarily using argon plasma coagulation and clipping-while gel immersion endoscopy helps secure the visual field. In hereditary polyposis syndromes (e.g., Peutz-Jeghers syndrome and familial adenomatous polyposis), endoscopic ischemic and cold snare polypectomy prevent intussusception and reduce cancer risk, decreasing surgical needs. Additionally, endoscopic balloon dilation is an established bowel-preserving treatment for fibrotic CD strictures, reducing surgical resection and short bowel syndrome risk. Driven by evolving imaging and devices, BAE remains central to small bowel management, improving patient outcomes and quality of life.

title: Recent advances in functionalized electrospun nanofibers for biomedical and therapeutic applications: A comprehensive review.
authors: Deshmukh K, Pandey M, Moulahoum H, Ghorbanizamani F, Kovářík T, Przekora-Kuśmierz A, Jena H, Vora M
abstract: Electrospun nanofibers (ESNFs) have become a major focus of modern research given their adaptable architecture, extensive interface, and distinctive physicochemical characteristics, making them appropriate for varied applications such as catalysis and environmental cleanup, drug delivery (DD), tissue engineering (TE), sensing, actuation, and various energy-related technologies. As a result, electrospinning (ES) has emerged as a versatile manufacturing technique, driving intensive efforts to engineer nanofibrous structures specifically for biomedical purposes. Functionalization of ESNFs can be achieved by embedding functional agents or altering surface chemistry to introduce specific functionalities. This review discusses the fabrication methods, optimization techniques, and broad biomedical applications of modified ESNFs, emphasizing their key properties, including biocompatibility, degradability, and safety profile. The article outlines various strategies for creating and modifying ESNFs, followed by a comprehensive analysis of their applications in tissue regeneration, DD, wound repair, antimicrobial therapy, cancer diagnostics and treatment, and biosensing. By critically evaluating recent advances, highlighting future directions, and addressing ongoing challenges about ES, this review underscores the transformative potential of functionalized ESNFs as efficient and adaptable biomaterials for biomedical technologies.

title: Spatial mechanopriming of multicellular interfaces drives cytoskeletal-to-nuclear remodeling to boost therapeutic efficacy of stem cells.
authors: Bayaraa O, Lee NH, Kim SH, Lee H, Li CJ, Fu X, Hyun J, Choi G
abstract: Engineering multicellular constructs through biophysical cues, independent of soluble biochemical factors, is a promising strategy to boost the therapeutic potential of stem cells for regenerative medicine. However, the mechanisms by which spatially organized cell-cell and cell-matrix interfaces govern multicellular signaling and subsequent behavioral outcomes remain poorly understood. Here, we elucidate these mechanistic events by introducing 2D nanoplates (∼350 nm) compartmentalized within the intercellular space of mesenchymal stem cell (MSC) spheroids to form de novo cell-matrix spatial interfaces. These interfaces redistribute internal stress across the spheroid, amplifying integrin-cytoskeleton-nucleus force transmission and restoring YAP-dependent mechanotransduction to achieve spatial mechanopriming. Cells within these mechanoprimed spheroids exhibit profound nuclear deformation, epigenetic remodeling, and spatially patterned metabolic activation. Finite element modeling and spatial transcriptomic analyses further reveal a spheroid-wide reorganization of cytoskeletal and transcriptional networks. Mechanistically, elevated cytoskeletal tension across the reorganized interfaces is associated with a putative, tension-associated pseudo-hypoxic signature involving HIF-1α-related signaling, establishing a mechanometabolic niche that robustly enhances angiogenic secretion. Consequently, mechanoprimed spheroids demonstrate superior engraftment, accelerated vascular regeneration, and improved perfusion recovery in a murine ischemia model. Collectively, this work establishes spatial mechanopriming as an effective strategy to remodel cytoskeletal-to-nuclear mechanics and enhance the therapeutic potential of 3D multicellular systems.

title: Injectable bioactive glass hydrogels orchestrate metalloimmunotherapy by depleting pathogenic B cells and rescuing bone in rheumatoid arthritis.
authors: Yan Z, Chen Y, Zeng F, Chen Q, Cai H, Qin R, Xu J, Gu B
abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is characterized by persistent synovial inflammation and progressive bone destruction. Transcriptomic profiling identified hyperactivated B cells as key contributors to osteoimmune dysregulation, supporting localized B cell intervention as a therapeutic strategy. Here, an injectable thermosensitive hydroxypropyl chitin hydrogel incorporating Cu/Zn-doped bioactive glass particles, termed BG@HPCH, was developed for localized metalloimmunotherapy. BG incorporation improved the shear-thinning behavior, thermosensitive gelation, storage modulus, and stability of the hydrogel. In vitro, ionic release from BG@HPCH selectively reduced pathogenic B cell survival while preserving mesenchymal stem cell (MSC) viability. The optimized M-BG@HPCH increased the B cell dead-cell area from 1.93 ± 0.48% to 91.12 ± 0.90% at 24 h, while maintaining MSC viability at 98.59 ± 0.26% after 3 days. In TNF-transgenic mice, a single intra-articular injection of BG@HPCH reduced arthritis index scores from 2.88 ± 0.18 to 1.81 ± 0.13 at day 28, limited bone erosion, and showed no detectable systemic toxicity. Micro-CT analysis showed improved bone preservation, with BV/TV increasing from 30.00 ± 6.74% to 55.66 ± 1.07%. OCN staining further confirmed enhanced osteogenic activity, with the OCN+ area increasing by 2.16 times. Flow cytometry confirmed reduced B220+CD45.2+ B cell accumulation in treated joints. Single-cell RNA sequencing of 23,921 joint cells showed that BG@HPCH reduced inflammatory B cell, macrophage, and fibroblast subsets while expanding osteoblast-associated regenerative populations, accompanied by suppression of CD23- and CD74-associated B cell signaling axes. These findings establish BG@HPCH as a localized immunoregenerative biomaterial for coordinating pathogenic B cell depletion and bone repair in RA.

title: A GelMA hydrogel co-loaded with ursolic acid, ferulic acid and naringin facilitates dentin regeneration by providing a multi-component odontogenic microenvironment.
authors: Che J, Yang A, Mo F, Gao Y, Li Y, Cui Y, Zhuo F, Hong Y
abstract: Dental caries is a prevalent bacterial infectious disease, yet current clinical treatments remain limited because conventional restorative materials provide only mechanical filling and fail to induce dental tissue regeneration. Herein, we developed a composite gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA) hydrogel system (Gel/UFN) co-loaded with three active components from traditional Chinese medicine, including ursolic acid (UA), ferulic acid (FA) and naringin (Nar), to remodel the carious microenvironment and promote dentin remineralization and vascularized pulp-dentin-like tissue formation. Gel/UFN showed excellent biocompatibility and favorable physicochemical and mechanical properties for dental applications, supporting adhesion and proliferation of human dental pulp stem cells (hDPSCs). Functionally, Gel/UFN significantly inhibited Streptococcus mutans (S. mutans) growth and biofilm formation, downregulated inflammatory cytokine expression and promoted the migration and angiogenesis of human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs). More importantly, Gel/UFN upregulated odontogenesis-related genes in hDPSCs, thereby enhancing odontogenic differentiation, alkaline phosphatase activity, collagen maturation and regenerative mineralization. In vivo, Gel/UFN exhibited slow degradation and sustained drug release for over 55 days. After implantation of Gel/UFN-filled dentin discs into nude mice, H&E staining demonstrated the formation of vascular structures, dentin-like mineralized tissue and cell-rich pulp-like tissue. Western blot analysis further revealed increased expression of the odontogenesis-related proteins RUNX2, DSPP, DMP1, and COL1A1 in the Gel/UFN group, providing additional protein-level evidence of its pro-odontogenic effects in vivo. These newly formed tissues were observed to cover exposed dentinal tubules on the surface of dentin disc using scanning electron microscopy (SEM). Micro-CT further confirmed that dental tissue induced by Gel/UFN exhibited a higher remineralization density at the defect site, supporting enhanced dentin remineralization. Overall, Gel/UFN may serve as a promising bioactive hydrogel platform for dentin repair and vascularized pulp-dentin-like tissue formation through antibacterial, anti-inflammatory, pro-angiogenic and pro-differentiation effects.

title: Iron-quercetin-incorporated PCL/PEO nanofibrous scaffolds for ADSC secretome modulation and in vitro regenerative responses.
authors: Daranarong D, Kantapan J, Jenvoraphot T, Innuan P, Rolin G, Viennet-Steiner C, Roytrakul S, Punyodom W
abstract: Chronic and non-healing wounds remain a major clinical challenge due to impaired angiogenesis and insufficient regenerative signaling. Although mesenchymal stem cell (MSC)-derived secretomes offer promise as cell-free therapeutics, clinical translation is hindered by limited regenerative potency and poor localization. Here, we translated Iron-Quercetin complex (IronQ) into a scaffold-integrated priming platform by developing IronQ-incorporated polycaprolactone/poly(ethylene oxide) (PCL/PEO) electrospun nanofibers for adipose-derived stem cell (ADSC) culture and secretome modulation. The optimized PCL/PEO (3:1) scaffold exhibited favorable architecture, mechanical properties, cytocompatibility, and pH-/temperature-responsive IronQ release. Proteomic and cytokine analyses demonstrated that nanofibrous scaffold-based culture, together with IronQ-mediated biochemical stimulation, was associated with changes in ADSC secretory profiles involving extracellular matrix organization and regenerative pathways, with increased levels of selected regenerative mediators, including VEGF-A, HGF, FGF-21, PDGF-AA, SDF-1α, and CCL-2. Functionally, conditioned medium generated from ADSCs cultured on the IronQ-containing scaffold enhanced endothelial proliferation and vascular network formation, as well as fibroblast responses associated with tissue repair in vitro. These findings support the potential of this bioactive nanofibrous platform as a scaffold-based strategy for modulating ADSC paracrine responses relevant to wound-healing applications.

title: Targeting the lactate/P300/H3K18la epigenetic pathway with a mechanoadaptive biomimetic hydrogel to suppress traumatic tendon heterotopic ossification.
authors: Feng H, Ang K, Deng Z, Cui C, Chen J, Huang N, Feng Y, Zhang J
abstract: Traumatic heterotopic ossification (HO) is a debilitating complication of tendon injury, yet its pathogenic mechanisms remain elusive and effective preventive strategies are lacking. Here, we identify a glycometabolic-epigenetic axis that drives HO progression. Single-cell profiling and functional analyses reveal that hypoxic chondrocytes undergo glycolytic reprogramming, leading to lactate accumulation and transfer into tendon-derived mesenchymal stem cells (TD-MSCs) through MCT1. This metabolic coupling promotes P300-dependent histone H3 lysine 18 lactylation (H3K18la), activating osteogenic programs characterized by Col6a1, Zhx3, Lox and Vdr expression and thereby facilitating pathological endochondral ossification. Guided by this mechanism, we develop a tendon-adhesive hydrogel (GelHA-A485@Exos) that integrates mechanical repair with targeted epigenetic modulation. MSC-derived exosomes enable localized delivery of the P300 inhibitor A485, suppressing H3K18la and aberrant osteogenic activation, while the hydrogel scaffold enhances tendon regeneration. In vivo and in vitro studies demonstrate that GelHA-A485@Exos promotes tendon healing while preventing HO formation. Our findings establish metabolic-epigenetic communication as a central regulator of traumatic HO and provide a translational therapeutic strategy for its clinical prevention.

title: Cascade DNA walker-driven photo-controlled CRISPR/Cas12a nanorobot enabling ultrasensitive one-pot detection of dual miRNAs in triple-negative breast cancer.
authors: Yu L, Li X, Huang L
abstract: MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are critical biomarkers for the early diagnosis of triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), but sensitive simultaneous detection of multiple miRNAs remains a clinical challenge. Herein, we report an innovative biosensing method based on a cascade DNA walker-driven photo-controlled CRISPR/Cas12a nanorobot for one-pot, rapid, and ultrasensitive dual miRNA detection. Target miRNAs trigger the cascade DNA walker, which integrates catalytic hairpin assembly and enzyme-mediated strand displacement, to generate abundant single-stranded DNA (ssDNA). These ssDNA then activate the photo-controlled CRISPR/Cas12a nanorobot under light illumination, enabling amplified fluorescence signaling for dual-target quantification. The assay exhibits a linear range of 100 aM to 1 pM with a limit of detection of 48.7 aM. Serum recovery experiments and cell line tests confirm its reliability in complex matrices. Clinical validation using 30 plasma samples (15 TNBC patients, 15 healthy controls) demonstrates high diagnostic accuracy (area under the curve, AUC = 0.964). This method features simple operation and strong clinical translational potential, offering a reliable tool for the early diagnosis of TNBC.

title: Teclistamab versus lenalidomide-dexamethasone in high-risk smoldering multiple myeloma: a randomized phase 2 trial.

title: Circulatory arrest versus aortic cross-clamping in proximal thoracic aortic aneurysm repair.
authors: Braatz E, Stenman M, Al-Mousli J, Dalén M, Olsson C
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Aortic cross‑clamping and mild hypothermic circulatory arrest (MHCA) are commonly used strategies in proximal thoracic aortic aneurysm surgery. This study compared these approaches in elective procedures for patients with a distal ascending aortic diameter of 40-50 mm. The primary outcome was a composite of 30‑day mortality, stroke, or acute kidney injury, with secondary outcomes including long‑term survival and postoperative complications. MATERIAL AND METHODS: This single‑center observational cohort included patients treated between 2016 and 2024. Distal ascending aortic diameters were assessed on preoperative computed tomography, and clinical data were obtained from SWEDEHEART. Patients were assigned to aortic cross‑clamp (n = 261) or MHCA (n = 138). Propensity score matching was performed in a 1:1 ratio to balance baseline characteristics. RESULTS: The composite primary outcome occurred in 15 patients (3.8%) and was more common with MHCA than with cross‑clamp (6.5% vs 2.3%, p = 0.035). Two patients (0.5%), both in the MHCA group, died within 30 days. After matching, the odds ratio for the composite endpoint was 2.4 (95% CI, 0.66-11.5), indicating no significant difference. Long‑term survival was similar between groups (log‑rank p = 0.33). CONCLUSIONS: Both strategies were associated with low perioperative risk and comparable long‑term survival. These results support flexible operative planning, allowing the distal anastomotic technique to be chosen based on individual anatomy and surgical preference.

title: Integrated analysis identifies dysregulated secretory proteins and crotonylation profiles associated with immune regulation in IgA nephropathy.
authors: Chen J, Zhang W, Dai Y, Ma H, Ma J, Zou G, Yan Q, Hu G
abstract: BACKGROUND: Immunoglobulin A nephropathy (IgAN) is the most prevalent primary glomerulonephritis worldwide, with 20%-40% of patients progressing to end-stage renal disease. However, the relationship between peripheral immune alterations and local renal injury, particularly with respect to the abundance patterns and post-translational modification signals of secretory proteins, remains incompletely characterized. METHODS: This study included 48 samples, consisting of renal tissue samples from 7 IgAN patients and 10 controls, and peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from 6 patients with IgAN and 25 controls. Renal tissue and PBMC samples were analyzed by proteomic and crotonylation profiling, respectively. These datasets represent cohort-level feature integration rather than paired multi-omics correlation analyses performed within the same individuals. Immune secretory protein annotations from the Human Protein Atlas supported downstream interpretation. Differential abundance analysis, protein-protein interaction (PPI) network analysis, functional enrichment, transcription factor (TF) prediction, and compound enrichment analysis using the DSigDB and Enrichr platforms were performed to explore molecular features and database-derived compounds associated with IgAN. RESULTS: Compared with the corresponding control groups, 92 differentially abundant secreted proteins and 36 secretory proteins with differential protein-abundance-normalized Kcr signals were identified in IgAN patients. PPI network analysis prioritized FGA, FGB, A2M, APOA1, C3, HP, SERPINA1, APOB, FGG, and TF as exploratory hub candidates, while STAT1, PML, STAT5B, and MYH11 were computationally predicted as candidate upstream TFs. Compound enrichment analysis identified thapsigargin as a database-derived, hypothesis-generating compound related to the secretory protein network in IgAN. CONCLUSIONS: This study provides an integrative characterization of secretory protein abundance and crotonylation patterns in IgA nephropathy. The findings suggest candidate hub proteins and upstream TFs potentially associated with immune dysregulation in IgAN. Despite the limited sample size, these results offer exploratory molecular insights and provide a basis for future mechanistic and experimental studies. SIGNIFICANCE: Secretory proteins may contribute to immune dysregulation and renal injury in immunoglobulin A nephropathy (IgAN), but their abundance patterns and lysine crotonylation (Kcr)-related features remain incompletely characterized. This study integrated renal tissue proteomics, peripheral blood mononuclear cell crotonylomics, public transcriptomics, and Human Protein Atlas annotations at the feature level across independent cohorts. Descriptive fold-change screening yielded 92 HPA-annotated secretory proteins in renal tissue and 36 secretory proteins containing 120 protein-abundance-normalized Kcr sites in peripheral blood mononuclear cells. Network analysis prioritized ten exploratory hub candidates, while STAT1, PML, STAT5B, and MYH11 were computationally prioritized as candidate upstream transcription factors. DSigDB/Enrichr analysis further highlighted thapsigargin as a database-derived enrichment signal for hypothesis generation. These findings provide an exploratory molecular resource for investigating secretory protein abundance and Kcr-related patterns in IgAN. Because the datasets were unpaired and the proteomic and crotonylomic samples were pooled within groups, the results do not establish participant-level cross-tissue relationships, causal regulation, validated biomarkers, or therapeutic efficacy. Larger individual-level cohorts and functional studies are required for validation.

title: ALMS1 stabilizes the proximal centriole to drive transition zone assembly and ciliogenesis.
authors: Phan TP, Derderian C, Herranz-Pérez V, Li KH, Burlingame AL, Reiter JF
abstract: The human ciliopathy Alström syndrome is caused by mutations in ALMS1. How ALMS1 contributes to cilia function has been unclear. Unlike other ciliopathy-associated proteins, ALMS1 localizes to the proximal end of centrioles, raising the possibility that it contributes to cilia function via a distinct mechanism. We found that, without ALMS1, centrioles are short and frequently break at their proximal ends. Truncated, broken ALMS1 mutant centrioles display reduced microtubule-organizing activity and disrupted centriole linkers. Without ALMS1, Golgi-derived cargos, including transmembrane components of the transition zone, are impaired in their trafficking to the centrosome. Consequently, ALMS1 is important for transition zone assembly, ciliogenesis, and the control of ciliary membrane composition. In mice, disruption of ALMS1 causes progressive, age-dependent loss of cilia in tissues affected in Alström syndrome, including retina, kidney, and brain. We conclude that Alström syndrome is caused by disruption of proximal centriole integrity and centrosome-directed protein trafficking, compromising ciliary assembly and maintenance.

title: Deficiency of NBAS causes immune dysregulation due to hyperactivation of IFN signaling.
authors: Liu C, Zhang L, Lu M, Shen Y, Yao Y, Liu F, Wang Q, Zhang B
abstract: NBAS deficiency is a multisystem disorder, but its immunologic manifestations and underlying mechanisms remain poorly defined. Here, we expand the genotypic and phenotypic spectrum of NBAS deficiency through four patients carrying five loss-of-function NBAS mutations. Minigene assays and RNA analysis showed that these splicing or missense mutations resulted in aberrant alternative splicing. Clinically, the patients showed early-onset recurrent or persistent cytopenias and immune dysregulation, together with severe infections, inflammatory activation, and multi-organ involvement, including renal and neurologic manifestations. Transcriptomic analysis revealed overactivation of type I interferon signaling pathways compared with healthy controls, and single-cell RNA sequencing demonstrated that this upregulated inflammation was predominantly driven by myeloid cells. Together, these findings identify NBAS deficiency as a cause of immune dysregulation characterized by myeloid-driven type I interferonopathy, expand the clinical spectrum of NBAS-related disorders, and highlight the critical role of NBAS in maintaining immune homeostasis.

Gut microbiota and metabolic characteristics in PWHIV with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD).
authors: Liu H, Xu T, Guo Y, Zhou X, Yan C, Zhu B, Xie Y
abstract: The global prevalence of Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) among persons with HIV (PWHIV) is estimated at 34%. This study examined the influence of gut microbial and metabolic alterations in PWHIV with MASLD. We conducted 16S rRNA sequencing on 60 fecal samples (24 from HIV group and 36 from HIV-MASLD group) to assess microbial composition, and employed LC/MS-based metabolomics on both fecal and plasma samples to identify variations in metabolites. An exploratory analysis was performed to compare plasma cytokines and oxidative stress markers between the two groups. Sequencing in the HIV-MASLD group showed lower Faecalibacterium and Anaerobutyricum, and higher Klebsiella, Escherichia, and Enterococcus. Metabolomic analysis revealed a reduction in anti-inflammatory metabolites (Dodecanedioic acid, 5-Phenylvaleric acid, Kynurenic acid) and antioxidant metabolites, coupled with an increase in the pro-inflammatory metabolite Gamma-Glutamyl-L-Putrescine in the HIV-MASLD group. And plasma analysis indicated a decline in 20-carboxy arachidonic acid. Additionally, Faecalibacterium and Anaerobutyricum correlated positively with anti-inflammatory metabolites, while Klebsiella, Enterobacter, and Citrobacter correlated negatively. Furthermore, Faecalibacterium and Anaerobutyricum also showed a moderate negative correlation with MDA levels. A random forest model using plasma metabolites showed the optimal discriminative ability for HIV-MASLD (AUC = 0.819 ± 0.0059). Differences in gut microbiota and metabolites in PWHIV may affect MASLD progression by influencing inflammation and oxidative stress. Modulating gut microbiota, such as adding Faecalibacterium and Anaerobutyricum, could be a treatment strategy for HIV-MASLD. Plasma metabolites have potential as noninvasive markers.

title: Heterojunction nanozyme achieve highly efficient antibacterial by cuproptosis-like death and ferroptosis-like death.
authors: Wang W, Zhu R, Gui H, Jin X, Wei X, Wang X
abstract: Metal-ion-mediated lethal pathways offers a highly potent strategy for antibacterial treatments. However, relying on single-pathway mechanisms often fails to overwhelm bacterial antioxidant defenses, reducing antibacterial efficacy. This study designed a heterojunction nanozyme (Cu2O/Fe2O3) that induces ferroptosis-like death and copper-mediated metabolic toxicity exhibiting cuproptosis-like features, achieving highly effective antibacterial treatment. Computational chemistry analysis indicates that the Cu2O/Fe2O3 heterointerface establishes a built-in electric field through spontaneous interfacial electron transfer, thereby enhancing its peroxidase (POD)-like activity. Within the acidic bacterial microenvironment, Cu2O/Fe2O3 catalyzes the generation of large amounts of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and releases metal ions, inducing and amplifying ferroptosis-like death, which disrupts the function of ETC enzymes by attacking iron-sulfur clusters. Concurrently, copper ions disrupt the redox balance by depleting bacillithiol (BSH), indirectly increasing bacterial susceptibility and promoting ferroptosis-like death. Furthermore, the accumulation of copper ions triggers severe metabolic impairments that biochemically resemble the cuproptosis cascade, which disrupts key enzymes of the TCA cycle and impairs the synthesis of electron donors (NADH and FADH2), thereby cutting off the supply of substrates to ETC at the upstream stage. Overall, this study demonstrates that triggering bimetallic ion-mediated metabolic disruptions induces an energy crisis in bacteria, providing a reference for multimodal antibacterial strategies.

title: Label-free impedimetric immunosensor for TSH detection using Ni-Co3O4/AuNP-modified screen-printed electrodes.
authors: Panda M, Swetha R, Krishna Priya M, Divya KP, Satheesh Babu TG, Pradeep A
abstract: Rapid, accessible, and accurate detection of thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) is essential for early diagnosis and effective management of thyroid disorders. This study reports the development of a label-free impedimetric immunosensor for TSH detection using flexible screen-printed carbon electrodes modified with Ni-Co3O4/AuNP. The developed sensor exhibits a wide linear detection range from 0.001 to 100 μIU/mL and a low limit of detection (LOD) of 0.001 μIU/mL, demonstrating a high sensitivity for TSH quantification. The sensor demonstrates excellent selectivity, reproducibility, and its performance is validated using serum samples, yielding recovery rates between 92.2 and 99.6%. The developed Ni-Co3O4/AuNP-based impedimetric immunosensor holds promise as a sensitive platform for point-of-care quantification of thyroid function.

title: 3D culture-derived MSC EV facilitate repair by activating microglial autophagy in spinal cord injury.
authors: Liu H, Li X, Li M, Jiu J, Zhao Y, Li D, Zhang J, Yan L
abstract: Spinal cord injury (SCI) is characterized by persistent neuroinflammation, neuronal loss, and limited tissue repair. Extracellular vesicles derived from human umbilical cord mesenchymal stromal cells (hUC-MSC-EVs) represent a promising cell-free therapeutic approach, although strategies for improving their bioactivity and regulating their cargo composition remain incompletely defined. Here, a gelatin microcarrier-based three-dimensional (3D) culture system was used to generate hUC-MSC-EVs. Compared with EVs generated under conventional two-dimensional (2D) culture conditions, 3D EVs reduced lesion severity, improved functional recovery, and promoted reparative-like changes in ionized calcium-binding adaptor molecule 1(Iba1)-positive microglia/macrophages in a rat SCI model. Transcriptomic, tandem-reporter, and pharmacological analyses indicated that intact autophagic processing contributes to the reparative-like phenotypic effects of 3D EVs in microglial cells. Comparative microRNA (miRNA) profiling identified miRNA-99a-5p as one of the enriched candidates, and gain- and loss-of-function experiments supported its contribution to autophagy-related and phenotype-associated responses in recipient microglia. The 3D culture condition was accompanied by increased nuclear localization of Yes-associated protein (YAP) and transcriptional coactivator with PDZ-binding motif (TAZ), increased expression of Y-box binding protein 1 (YBX1), TEA domain transcription factor 4 (TEAD4) occupancy at selected YBX1 promoter regions, and higher EV-associated miR-99a-5p abundance. RNA immunoprecipitation (RIP) analysis further demonstrated an association between YBX1 and miR-99a-5p. Overall, these findings indicate that 3D culture is associated with EV cargo remodeling and improved therapeutic effects after SCI, while miR-99a-5p represents one functional EV-associated cargo contributing to selected microglial responses.

title: Sulfur-doped graphitic carbon nitride/cerium tungstate nanocomposites for ultrasensitive dopamine sensing in mouse striatal tissue.
authors: Jang HG, Manikandan R, Moon SM, Mugunthan UA, Lee J, Kang GW, Park J, Yoon JH
abstract: Following the COVID-19 pandemic, the demand for rapid diagnostic tools for the highly specific and sensitive detection of disease-related biomarkers has increased significantly. Hybrid nanocomposite-modified disposable screen-printed electrodes have shown remarkable potential for the electrochemical biosensing of various biomarkers. This study reports the fabrication of a hybrid nanocomposite comprising sulfur-doped graphitic carbon nitride (S-g-C3N4) nanosheets integrated with two-dimensional cerium tungstate (CeW) for highly sensitive electrochemical dopamine detection. The synthesized S-g-C3N4@CeW hybrid nanocomposite was thoroughly characterized using field-emission scanning electron microscopy coupled with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy, Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy, and electrochemical measurements. Electroanalytical performance was evaluated using differential pulse voltammetry (DPV) under optimized experimental conditions. The fabricated electrochemical sensor exhibited a wide linear concentration range for dopamine from 0.1 to 500 μM, with a low detection limit of 1.13 nM and high sensitivity of 151.69 μA μM-1 cm-2. Finally, the fabricated sensor was used for the ex-vivo determination of dopamine in Parkinson's disease-induced mouse striatum-tissue samples, achieving good accuracy with recovery rates of 92.0 to 101.4%. This study demonstrates a promising strategy for fabricating hybrid nanocomposite-modified disposable electrochemical sensors for neurotransmitter detection in animal-disease models.

title: Sex-divergent vulnerability to chronic peripheral LPS challenge in aged ApoE4 mice: Male systemic fragility versus female central neuroinflammation.
authors: Barberà-Parada S, Biosca-Brull J, Gabaldón-Díaz R, Rodulfo-Cárdenas R, Guardia-Escoté L, Blanco J, Cabré M, Colomina MT
abstract: Inflammageing links chronic inflammation to biological aging, contributing to senescence and multimorbidity common in the elderly. In neurodegenerative diseases, such as Alzheimer's disease, inflammatory processes play a causal role in accelerating neurodegeneration. Interestingly, apolipoprotein E (APOE), particularly the APOEε4 allele, is a major genetic risk factor for neurodegeneration, acting as a key immunomodulator with sex differences. This is especially relevant given the lack of clear prevention strategies for APOEε4 carriers. Therefore, this study characterized the sex-specific neuroinflammatory and cognitive vulnerability of APOE4 genotype under a chronic lipopolysaccharide (LPS) challenge in senescence-transition stage. Male and female homozygous apoE4 mice (15-16 months old) were administered intraperitoneal doses of 0 or 0.25 mg/kg LPS three times per week for a total of 17 doses. Body weight was monitored, and behavioural assessments were conducted from the 12th injection until the 17th. Serum and tissues were collected to assess hippocampal, cortical and systemic markers of inflammation, antioxidant-related genes, genes implied in myelin dynamics, and neurotrophin-related transcripts. Findings revealed basal sex-dependent divergent phenotypes with specific responses under LPS challenge. Under LPS treatment, males exhibited higher systemic fragility, with significantly increased mortality, which may have conditioned cognitive outcomes. Females showed greater central alterations related to neuroinflammation along with altered expression of myelin-related transcripts. However, the results suggest a stablished tolerance to LPS. These results highlight how chronic systemic inflammation during ageing in an APOE4 genotype background shapes sex-divergent pathological trajectories, underscoring the need to address sex-specific therapeutic strategies.

title: Acute Pancreatitis Caused by Impaction of Migrated Surgical Staples in the Duodenal Papilla After Distal Pancreatectomy.
authors: Inaba K, Motomura M, Azuma Y, Kimoto T, Takahashi H, Ueo T, Narita R, Tada K
abstract: A 67-year-old woman underwent a laparoscopic distal pancreatectomy for pancreatic body cancer. On postoperative day (POD) 23, the patient presented with epigastric pain and was diagnosed with delayed peripancreatic fluid collection, which was treated with antibiotics and percutaneous drainage. On POD 51, the patient developed recurrent epigastric pain. Laboratory tests revealed elevated pancreatic enzyme and inflammatory marker levels. Computed tomography revealed acute pancreatitis and a high-density area in the duodenal papilla suggestive of a foreign body. Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography revealed that the surgical staples were impacted in the minor duodenal papilla and were successfully removed. Although pancreatography did not demonstrate residual staples, three additional staples were subsequently removed from the pancreatic duct. Pancreatitis improved after endoscopic treatment, and the patient was discharged. This case suggests that the migration of staples used during surgery may be a contributing factor to postoperative pancreatitis.

title: Prevalence and Clinical Significance of Gastric-Type Mucosal Lesions in Non-Ampullary Duodenal Epithelial Tumors Based on Mucin Phenotype.
authors: Ohno K, Nakatani E, Kurokami T, Kawai A, Matsuda M, Masui Y, Satoh T, Hirata T
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Non-ampullary duodenal epithelial tumors differ in clinicopathological features according to mucin phenotype. Gastric-type tumors have distinct biological features; however, their associated mucosal background remains unclear. In this study, gastric foveolar metaplasia, gastric heterotopia, and Brunner's gland hyperplasia were collectively referred to as gastric-type mucosal lesions (G-MLs). We aimed to assess their prevalence and associations with mucin phenotype and clinicopathological factors. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed the data of 130 patients with 130 resected non-ampullary duodenal epithelial tumors at a single center. Tumors were classified according to mucin phenotype. The prevalence of concomitant G-MLs and associated factors was evaluated. Exploratory Firth-penalized logistic regression analysis was used to assess the association between gastric-type tumors and G-ML presence. RESULTS: Concomitant G-MLs were identified in 44 patients (33.8%). Their prevalence was higher in gastric-type tumors (13/16; 81.3%) than in gastric-intestinal-type tumors (10/37; 27.0%) and intestinal-type tumors (21/77; 27.3%). G-MLs were associated with mild endoscopic gastric mucosal atrophy and smoking status and were inversely associated with current Helicobacter pylori infection. In the exploratory fully adjusted model, gastric-type tumors remained positively associated with the presence of G-MLs (adjusted odds ratio, 7.00; 95% confidence interval, 1.98-30.95; p = 0.002). CONCLUSIONS: G-MLs were present in approximately one-third of patients and were most frequent in gastric-type tumors. These findings indicate an association between G-MLs and gastric-type tumors; however, the cross-sectional design does not allow inference of a biological relationship. TRIAL REGISTRATION: N/A.

title: Inflammation-anchored injectable hydrogel integrating pathological nitric oxide scavenging and on-demand drug release for localized inflammatory bowel disease therapy.
authors: Eom S, Lee S, Boo Y, Kim J, Kim WJ
abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), encompassing chronic relapsing gastrointestinal disorders, remains a profound clinical challenge because conventional therapeutics are often impeded by systemic off-target toxicities and suboptimal retention at inflamed mucosal sites. Herein, an inflammation-activated and retentive injectable hydrogel is presented, which leverages pathological nitric oxide (NO) overproduction as both a therapeutic target and an autonomous release trigger. An NO-responsive and NO-scavenging polymer (NRSP) incorporating an NO-cleavable o-phenylenediamine (o-PD) motif is formulated into cationic, dexamethasone-encapsulating micelles and electrostatically assembled with anionic hyaluronic acid (HA) to form a shear-thinning hydrogel that facilitates minimally invasive rectal administration and ensures prolonged, localized retention at the inflamed mucosal interface. Upon exposure to the NO-rich inflammatory microenvironment, structural disruption of NO-responsive and NO-scavenging micelles (NRSM) compromises the electrostatic integrity of the HA-micelle network, thereby reducing the storage modulus and accelerating cargo release. In vitro evaluations using lipopolysaccharide-stimulated macrophages demonstrate that NRSM hydrogels effectively reduce intracellular and extracellular NO levels and attenuate pro-inflammatory cytokine secretion. Furthermore, the HA matrix mediates disease-adaptive localization through CD44 receptor recognition and preferential electrostatic adhesion to positively charged inflammatory interfaces, resulting in enhanced colonic retention in DSS-induced colitis models ex vivo. Following rectal administration in DSS-induced mice, NRSM-based hydrogels significantly alleviate disease severity, reduce colonic NO and inflammatory cytokine levels, and rescue mucosal architecture and mucin-associated features. Notably, dexamethasone-loaded NRSM hydrogel exerted the most potent synergistic therapeutic benefit. Overall, this disease-responsive hydrogel platform establishes an effective localized intervention for IBD, merging intrinsic pathological NO scavenging with controlled drug delivery.

title: Bioactive M2 exosome hybrid nanocomposites for immune therapy of psoriasis.
authors: Wei Y, Chen S, Yang N, Tao X, Zhang H, Zhao Y, Zhu Y, Gu Z
abstract: Psoriasis is a chronic autoimmune skin disease characterized by persistent oxidative stress and sustained inflammation, affecting approximately 1-8% of the global population, with no curative therapy has been well-established to date. To address this, we developed a bioactive hybrid nanocomposite (Exo-Ce) by chemically conjugating M2 macrophage-derived exosomes with cerium oxide nanoparticles (CeNP), which was applied for synergistic and immunomodulatory therapy of psoriasis. This nanohybrid system effectively integrates the natural immunomodulatory properties of exosomes with the reliable antioxidant enzyme-mimetic activities of CeNP. In vitro, mild thiol-maleimide click chemistry minimizes exosome damage; Exo-Ce maintains parental M2-exosome core bioactivity and exhibits ROS-scavenging capacity, significantly reducing intracellular ROS levels and suppressing the secretion of pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-6 and TNF-α). Following subcutaneous administration in an imiquimod (IMQ)-induced psoriasis mouse model, Exo-Ce markedly ameliorated psoriatic lesions, as evidenced by reduced lesional area, attenuated epidermal hyperkeratosis and acanthosis, and decreased immune cell infiltration. More specifically, Exo-Ce could promote the polarization of macrophages toward an anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype via its ROS-scavenging activity, as well as downregulate key psoriasis-associated cytokines (e.g., IL-1β and TNF-α), thereby facilitating the restoration of tissue homeostasis in vivo. Altogether, our findings position Exo-Ce as a biocompatible and synergistic nanohybrid platform for psoriasis immunotherapy, potentially offering a promising strategy for clinical translation.
